content.title: One grammar, three object kinds
content.lede: gowkhtmltopdf accepts wkhtmltopdf-style multi-object command lines: page, cover, and toc objects, each with their own flag scope, ending in a single output path.

content.heading: Usage grammar
content.code:
gowkhtmltopdf [GLOBAL OPTIONS] [OBJECT]... <output>
  OBJECT:
    [PAGE OPTIONS]  page <input>
    [TOC OPTIONS]   toc
    [COVER OPTIONS] cover <input>

  <output> is required; use "-" to write the PDF to stdout.
  <input> may be a file path, a URL, or "-" to read HTML from stdin.
  Local file reads are denied by default: pass --enable-local-file-access.

  Doc flags: -h/--help, -V/--version, -L/--license, -E/--extended-help.
  Short flags: -q (quiet), -g (grayscale), -O (orientation), -s (page-size),
               -T/-B/-L/-R (margins), -c (copies), -t (title).
  Exit codes: 0 success, 1 error, 2 HTTP 404, 3 HTTP 401.

  Example:
  gowkhtmltopdf --page-size A4 --margin-top 15mm report.html out.pdf

sections.heading: Two scopes, one grammar
sections.body: Global flags (parsed into `settings.PdfGlobal` in `internal/cli/flags.go`) apply to the whole document: `--page-size`, `--orientation`, `--margin-top/bottom/left/right`, `--page-width`, `--page-height`, `--grayscale`, `--copies`, `--collate`, `--title`, `--outline`, `--font-path`, `--quiet`. Page-scoped flags apply to one object only: `--zoom`, `--username`, `--password`, `--timeout`, `--external-links`, `--internal-links` are page-only flags routed through `pageOnlyFlag` in `internal/cli/flags.go`.
bullets: A page-scoped flag placed before any object keyword is parked as "pending" and promoted into the first real page or cover object, never into a `toc` object (`pending` in `objectCtx`, `internal/cli/cli.go`).
Header/footer flags before any object keyword stay global so every object inherits them (`hfFlag` in `internal/cli/flags.go`).
`--enable-local-file-access` is dual-home: it writes global `enablelocalfileaccess=true` and object `load.blocklocalfileaccess=false` through the `applyPage` router.

sections.heading: Concrete example
sections.body: In this invocation `--page-size` and `--orientation` land on the global settings, `--zoom 1.25` is collected as pending page settings, and `--enable-local-file-access` after the `page` keyword opens that page object:

content.heading: Cover + TOC + pages
content.code:
gowkhtmltopdf \
  --header-left "gowkhtmltopdf" --header-right "[title]" --header-line \
  --footer-center "[page] / [topage]" --footer-line \
  --toc-header-text "Report contents" --disable-dotted-lines \
  --outline --outline-depth 4 --title "Invoice Report" \
  cover --enable-local-file-access cover.html \
  toc \
  page --enable-local-file-access chapter1.html \
  page --enable-local-file-access chapter2.html \
  book.pdf

content.heading: Placeholder tokens for text headers and footers
items: `[frompage]` - first page number of the document
`[doctitle]` - the document title from the HTML `<title>` element
`[webpage]` - the source URL of the current page
`[section]` and `[subsection]` - the current TOC section and subsection heading
Custom tokens: `--replace name value` substitutes `[name]` with `value` in header and footer text (pair flag in `internal/cli/flags.go`)

content.heading: Flag categories
rows: Object after a keyword; global before any keyword
Current `toc` object; otherwise global for all TOC objects
Image global; PDF mode rejects them

content.title: Stdin and stdout
content.body: An output path of "-" writes the PDF bytes to stdout (`OpenOutput` in `internal/cli/cli.go`), and an input of "-" reads the HTML from stdin, so `cat report.html | gowkhtmltopdf --enable-local-file-access - - > report.pdf` works. Progress phases print to stderr unless `--quiet`, keeping stdout clean for the PDF bytes.
